slides.headline: He spent three years on one investigation - from Silicon Valley to China to the US border. It just won a Pulitzer.
Aniruddha Ghosal was part of the Associated Press team that won the 2026 Pulitzer Prize for International Reporting
slides.body: The prize, announced May 4, 2026, honoured an investigation into state-of-the-art mass surveillance tools - tracing their path from Silicon Valley, through development in China, to eventual use by US Border Patrol.

slides.headline: The investigation spanned three years, thousands of pages of documents, and numerous interviews.
slides.body: Ghosal, an AP reporter based in Hanoi covering business and climate in Southeast Asia, shared the prize with three other AP journalists and a contributor - one of the most prestigious honours in journalism.

slides.eyebrow: Why it matters for Viksit Bharat 2047
slides.headline: A Viksit Bharat benefits when its journalists hold global power to account, not just report on India.
slides.body: Ghosal's Pulitzer came from investigating surveillance technology's path across three continents - Indian-origin reporting talent working at the highest level of international accountability journalism.
